members.name: ContentSizer
members.signature: public ElementBuilder ContentSizer(Func<float?, float?, (float, float)?> sizer)

docs.summary: Sets a content sizing function for auto-sized elements. The function receives optional width and height constraints and should return the preferred content size. This is particularly useful for custom controls that need to calculate their own size based on content.
docs.example: // Example: Size based on text content .ContentSizer((maxWidth, maxHeight) => { var textSize = MeasureText("My content", font, fontSize); return (textSize.Width + padding * 2, textSize.Height + padding * 2); }) // Example: Aspect ratio sizing .ContentSizer((maxWidth, maxHeight) => { const float aspectRatio = 16.0 / 9.0; if (maxWidth.HasValue) { return (maxWidth.Value, maxWidth.Value / aspectRatio); } if (maxHeight.HasValue) { return (maxHeight.Value * aspectRatio, maxHeight.Value); } return (320, 180); // Default size })

params.sizer: Function that takes (maxWidth?, maxHeight?) and returns (preferredWidth, preferredHeight)?. Return null if the element cannot be sized with the given constraints.

Enables content clipping to the element's bounds.

Keeps raised layers inside this element. Descendants on a higher [`Layer`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Layer) still draw and take the pointer above their siblings, but within this element and its clip instead of over everything else. Useful for a UI drawn into a panel, a preview, or a scrolling list whose popups should stay put.

Clamps the element so it stays within the screen bounds. Applied after layout, before rendering. Works with both SelfDirected and ParentDirected elements. Children are moved with the parent automatically.
Places the element on a specific rendering layer. Higher values render on top of lower ones and are hit-tested first.

params.layer: Layer value. Use [`Base`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Layer~Base), [`Overlay`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Layer~Overlay), [`Topmost`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Layer~Topmost), or any custom `int` (e.g. `Layer.Overlay + 10` to wedge a new tier between the named ones).

docs.summary:
Draws this element's [`Text`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.ElementBuilder~Text) as rich text.

A tag is a name and optional arguments between angle brackets, and an empty closing tag ends the most recent one. Styling: `b`, `i`, `u`, `s`, `mono`, `size 1.5`, `link url`, and a colour as `#f80` or a name like `red`. Effects, each taking an optional strength, speed and `#colour`: `shake`, `wiggle`, `wave`, `sizewave`, `bounce`, `slide`, `dangle`, `pendulum`, `swing`, `rotate`, `pulse`, `rainbow`.

The faces are optional. A style whose face is missing falls back to the regular font.

docs.summary: Truncate single-line text with a trailing ellipsis ("...") when it's wider than the element. The ellipsis is guaranteed to fit; has no effect on wrapped (multi-line) text.

Flex-wrap the parent-directed children: when they overrun this element's main axis they flow onto a new line, and the element auto-grows on the cross axis to fit every line. Space them with Gap (between items) and LineGap (between lines). Cross-axis stretch is resolved against the wrapped line size. Use fixed or auto cross sizes for content-driven lines.
